reviews.title: The ling app is amazing
reviews.text:
Let’s be honest: learning a new language can feel completely overwhelming.


Whether you’re trying to pick up Thai for an upcoming trip, reconnecting with your roots through Tagalog, or diving into one of 60+ other options, staring at rigid grammar rules isn't the answer. That’s why the Ling Appskips the boring drills and focuses on getting you talking.
Instead of forcing you to memorize random words you’ll never actually use, Ling throws you right into real-life scenarios with interactive mini-games and real audio from native speakers. You even get to text and talk with an AI chatbot to practice conversations without any of the social anxiety. From nailing tricky writing scripts to actually getting your pronunciation right, it breaks everything down into fun, bite-sized daily habits. If you're ready to stop just playing games and start actually speaking a language, Ling is the tool to get you there.

reviews.title: Better than Duolingo and doesn't use AI, but harder to get started
reviews.text:
I took three years of French in high school, have used Duolingo a lot since, and then found this app. Naturally, I started with French since I already have a foundation for it, and that has gone great! Previously I mainly had the most luck with my reading and writing, and Ling has vastly improved my listening and speaking.

However, I have also started the Afrikaans course, having never had an opportunity for it before.

It is very difficult! You are started with simple phrases, which is a nice way to ease into it. However, without foundation and the ability to learn the individual words, it is much more difficult. I can learn lots of phrases, but without the ability to see what words individually mean what, it becomes difficult to learn new words through context. I would love it if a feature could be added to tap a specific word and see what it means. So far, this is the only downside I have found.

This isn’t user error - I’m Filipino and I practice Tagalog around my friends and family - so I’m not delusional about pronunciation. It just doesn’t pick up certain words *at all.* The playback feature is also broken most of the time - so it rejects part of your answer and won’t let you continue. Reporting the error also causes the app to freeze and become non responsive. So I’ve had to do the same lesson multiple times and stop reporting the bugs.

reviews.title: No Tamil speaker reviewed the Tamil course
reviews.text: I don’t know if they’re just Google translating or using AI or what but … this app doesn’t actually teach properly. Just for example, in English if you respond to someone’s “How are you?” by saying that you’re well, you can then say, “How’re you?” They teach you to say, “Ninga yeppadi?” (literally how you) which is nonsense in Tamil without an iruukinga. This is the most basic interaction in the language and they completely botched it, so there’s no reason to trust the rest of their course. Don’t 👏 release 👏 language 👏 courses 👏 without 👏 a 👏 native 👏 speaker 👏 reviewing 👏 them!!!
